note: Time Range provides a single field widget (id time_range, label 'Time range') for the core daterange field type. It stores no data of its own - it only changes the manage-form-display widget so that a Date range field renders as time-only start/end HTML5 inputs. Its two settings are start_label (default 'Start time') and end_label (default 'End time'), schema field.widget.settings.time_range. There is no configure route, no permissions, no drush. Medium cases create daterange fields on Article with the time_range widget configured and ask the agent to read back labels / which field uses the widget; hard cases require the agent to switch a field's widget to time_range and to set custom labels, verified against the live core.entity_form_display config. All fixtures use namespaced field_tr_* fields on the existing Article content type.

evals.prompt: What core field type does the Drupal time_range module's Time Range widget work with, and what does the widget hide compared to the default widget?
evals.expected_output: The Time range widget (id time_range) applies to the core daterange field type (a 'Date range' field with the Date and time type). It hides the date element and shows only start-time and end-time HTML5 time inputs.

evals.prompt: Which two settings does the time_range field widget expose on the Manage form display page, and what do they default to?
evals.expected_output: start_label (default 'Start time') and end_label (default 'End time'); they retitle the start and end time inputs. Schema field.widget.settings.time_range.

evals.prompt: Does the time_range module define its own field type and store time data, or is it only a widget? Where does the actual value live?
evals.expected_output: It is only a form widget; it does not define a field type or store data. Storage is provided by core's Date range (daterange) field. The widget only changes how the value is entered on the form.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the Article content type has a Date range field field_tr_known that uses the Time Range widget. Inspect the live default form display and report the start and end time labels configured for that widget.
evals.expected_output: The field_tr_known component in core.entity_form_display.node.article.default uses widget time_range with settings.start_label = 'Opens' and settings.end_label = 'Closes'.

evals.prompt: The Article content type on this site has two Date range fields, field_tr_which and field_tr_other. Exactly one of them uses the time_range module's Time Range widget on the default form. Inspect the live form-display configuration and state which field uses the Time Range widget.
evals.expected_output: field_tr_which uses widget time_range; field_tr_other uses the core daterange_default widget. Read core.entity_form_display.node.article.default.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the Article content type has a Date range field field_tr_task that currently uses the core Date range (daterange_default) widget. Using the time_range module, switch this field's widget on the default form display to the Time Range widget. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: In core.entity_form_display.node.article.default the field_tr_task component has type: time_range (set the component's widget to time_range and save).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the Article content type has a Date range field field_tr_shift that already uses the Time Range widget with the default labels. Configure that widget so the start input is labelled 'Shift start' and the end input is labelled 'Shift end'. Apply the change to the live default form display.
evals.expected_output: In core.entity_form_display.node.article.default the field_tr_shift component (type time_range) has settings.start_label: 'Shift start' and settings.end_label: 'Shift end'.
